# Vietnam Thermal Power Plant Inventory: Sector Overview

Vietnam's power sector has experienced rapid capacity expansion, with total installed generation capacity reaching approximately **77,000 MW by 2024**. Thermal power— predominantly coal, gas, and oil—constitutes the backbone of the system, accounting for nearly **55% of installed capacity** and **~65% of annual generation**.

## Generation Mix (2024)

- **Coal-fired**: ~26,000 MW (34% capacity, 46% generation) – predominantly subcritical and supercritical pulverized coal units, with emerging ultra-supercritical (USC) installations
- **Gas/LNG**: ~9,000 MW (12% capacity) – combined-cycle gas turbine (CCGT) plants using domestic offshore gas; first LNG-to-power projects under development
- **Oil**: <1,000 MW (legacy peaking units, largely decommissioned)
- **Hydro**: ~22,000 MW (28% capacity)
- **Renewables**: ~20,000 MW (26% capacity) – solar, wind, biomass

## Policy Framework and Thermal Targets

**Power Development Plan 7 (PDP7, 2011)** targeted coal capacity of 36,000 MW by 2020 and 75,000 MW by 2030. **PDP7 Adjustment (PDP7A, 2016)** revised coal downward and introduced strict environmental criteria. **PDP8 (Decision 500/QD-TTg, May 2023)** fundamentally reorients the sector:

- **Coal**: Peaks at **30,127 MW by 2030** then phase-out; no new coal plants after 2030
- **LNG**: **22,400 MW by 2030**, ramping from 2025 onwards via floating storage regasification units (FSRU) and onshore terminals
- **Domestic gas**: **14,930 MW by 2030**, contingent on declining offshore field output
- **Cogeneration**: **2,700 MW by 2030**, encouraged for industrial parks

## Fuel Supply Landscape

- **Domestic coal**: Vinacomin (TKV) supplies ~70% of coal burn (anthracite); production plateaued at ~40-45 Mt/year; quality declining
- **Imported coal**: ~30% of thermal coal needs, primarily imported by IPPs and BOT plants via seaborne deliveries
- **Domestic gas**: Nam Côn Sơn, Cửu Long, Báo Vàng fields; production declining 8-10% annually
- **LNG imports**: Thi Vai LNG terminal (1 MTPA, operational 2023), Son My LNG (2 MTPA, 2025+), Hai Phong LNG, Quang Ninh LNG terminals under development

## Institutional Actors

- **EVN**: State utility; owns transmission, distribution, and three GENCOs (GENCO1, GENCO2, GENCO3); ~40% of thermal capacity
- **PVN**: Vietnam Oil & Gas Group; dominates gas-fired generation portfolio; developing LNG infrastructure
- **Vinacomin (TKV)**: State coal miner; operates mine-mouth coal plants and supplies fuel
- **BOT Investors**: Korean (KEPCO, Samsung C&T), Japanese (Marubeni, Sumitomo, J-Power), Thai (EGATi, Gulf Energy), Malaysian (JAKS), Singaporean (Sembcorp, Janakuasa)
- **IPPs**: Formosa Plastics, An Khanh Energy, Thang Long Power, Hải Hà CHP, industrial cogeneration
